hints: The sample proportion is $\hat{p} = \dfrac{36}{120}$. The variance of a sample proportion is $\dfrac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n}$ with $n = 120$: put your numbers in.
An approximate confidence interval has the form $\hat{p} \pm z\sqrt{\text{variance}}$. Take the square root of the variance you just found: it is the standard deviation of $\hat{p}$.
For a 90% interval, 5% is left in each tail. Find the $z$ with $\Phi(z) = 0.95$ from your tables or calculator (inverse normal).
Work out $\hat{p} - z \times \text{(standard deviation)}$ and $\hat{p} + z \times \text{(standard deviation)}$, then round both ends to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
**What we are asked to do**

We want a confidence interval for a proportion: a range of values in which the true proportion of Hungton voters who back the Alpha party probably lies. The word *approximate* is there because we use a normal distribution to build it.

Some symbols. $n$ is the sample size, so $n = 120$. $\hat{p}$ (say "p-hat") is the **sample proportion**: the fraction of the sample who said yes.

**Find the sample proportion**

36 out of 120 voters said they would vote Alpha, so

$$\hat{p} = \frac{36}{120} = 0.3$$

**Find the variance of the sample proportion (this earns the first M1)**

The spread of a sample proportion is measured by its variance, $\dfrac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n}$. Put in the numbers one at a time.

$$1 - \hat{p} = 1 - 0.3 = 0.7$$

$$\hat{p}(1-\hat{p}) = 0.3 \times 0.7 = 0.21$$

$$\text{Var} = \frac{0.21}{120} = 0.00175$$

Quick check: the standard deviation is the square root of the variance, because variance is a squared quantity.

$$\sqrt{0.00175} = 0.041833\ldots$$

Keep this on your calculator (press the answer key) rather than typing a rounded value.

**Choose the $z$-value for 90% (this earns the B1)**

A 90% interval covers the middle 90% of the normal distribution. That leaves $100\% - 90\% = 10\%$ outside, split equally: 5% in each tail.

So the area to the left of the upper end is $1 - 0.05 = 0.95$. We need the $z$ with $\Phi(z) = 0.95$. Use the inverse normal on your calculator, or the percentage-points table.

$$z = 1.645$$

Common slip: using $0.90$ as if it were the $z$-value. The mark scheme says it must be a $z$-value, not a probability.

**Build the interval (this earns the second M1)**

The interval is $\hat{p} \pm z \times \text{standard deviation}$. First find the amount to add and subtract:

$$1.645 \times 0.041833 = 0.068816\ldots$$

Lower end:

$$0.3 - 0.068816 = 0.231184\ldots \approx 0.231$$

Upper end:

$$0.3 + 0.068816 = 0.368816\ldots \approx 0.369$$

Both are rounded to 3 significant figures, as the A1 requires.

**Final answer**

The approximate 90% confidence interval for the proportion of voters in Hungton who would vote for the Alpha party is

$$0.231 \text{ to } 0.369$$
